intended_object: The canonical duality equivalence: for a localizer morphism Φ : W₁ → W₂ and an object X₂ of C₂, the opposite of the category of left resolutions of X₂ is equivalent to the category of right resolutions of op X₂ for the opposite localizer morphism Φ.op. This is read off the docstring and the type.
explanation:
A left resolution of X₂ is an object X₁ of C₁ with a morphism w : Φ.functor X₁ ⟶ X₂ that lies in W₂. Passing to opposites turns it into w.op : op X₂ ⟶ Φ.op.functor (op X₁), which lies in W₂.op. That is exactly a right resolution of op X₂ for Φ.op, and morphisms of resolutions correspond in the same way.

The definition builds the equivalence from two functors. `opFunctor` sends L to L.op and φ to φ.unop.f.op. The inverse is `unopFunctor.rightOp`, built the same way in the other direction. The two composites are definitionally the identity, so the unit and counit are `Iso.refl`. This is the standard identification and matches the docstring.

The equivalence is stated for any categories and any localizer morphism, so it has no extra hypotheses and is not too narrow. Mathlib has no other declaration for this specific equivalence. The `set_option` lines only adjust elaboration and do not change what is defined.
